title: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy)
therapy_label: Antibody–drug conjugate · days 1 and 8 every 3 weeks
setting: Previously treated unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer
dose: 10 mg/kg intravenously on days 1 and 8 of a 21-day cycle; prescribed reductions may apply
schedule: Two treatment visits in each three-week cycle: Day 1, then Day 8. There is no planned infusion on Day 15. The next cycle starts after Day 21 if the team confirms it is appropriate.
administration: The first infusion takes about three hours; later infusions usually take one to two hours if the earlier infusion was tolerated. Premedicines, checks and at least 30 minutes of observation after every infusion add to the visit. No take-home infusion pump is part of this regimen.
duration: Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable. There is no fixed number of cycles; the oncology team reviews benefit, scans and tolerability.
indication: NCCP00794a covers adults with unresectable or metastatic triple-negative breast cancer after at least two prior systemic therapies, including at least one for advanced disease. The NCCP entry specifies ECOG 0–1. Broader European licensed indications must be checked separately against the applicable Irish regimen and reimbursement pathway.
purpose: To control the cancer, relieve or delay symptoms, and help people live longer. This advanced-disease regimen does not promise a cure or an individual duration of benefit.
baseline: Before the first treatment: full blood count, kidney and liver blood tests, glucose and electrolytes including magnesium, calcium and phosphate. Pregnancy testing is needed where relevant. ECG is added if clinically indicated. The team checks infection, medicines, previous low blood counts and whether preventive G-CSF injections are appropriate.
ongoing: Blood count, kidney and liver tests are checked before each cycle; the neutrophil count must also meet the separate Day 8 threshold before that infusion. Glucose and the listed electrolytes are checked every second cycle. Pregnancy testing is repeated before each cycle where relevant. Review diarrhoea, hydration, nausea, oral intake, fever and infection before each infusion. Scans follow the individual response-assessment plan.
heart: An ECG is used when clinically indicated. Sacituzumab alone does not require a routine echocardiogram schedule. Cardiac symptoms or other medicines may change the plan.
bone: A routine DXA scan is not a sacituzumab-specific requirement. Bone health, bone metastases and any bone-strengthening treatment need their own individual plan.
urgent: Contact the oncology service immediately for fever, shivering or feeling acutely unwell; significant diarrhoea, inability to keep fluids down, dizziness, very little urine, or abdominal pain. Do not wait for the next treatment visit. During an infusion, tell staff immediately about breathing difficulty, swelling, rash, chest discomfort or faintness. Use the emergency service for severe breathing difficulty, collapse or other life-threatening symptoms.
special: Blood-count rules differ between Day 1 and Day 8. Known reduced UGT1A1 activity may increase side effects, but routine genotype testing is not required by the EU product information. Important differences between the NCCP and current EU dose-modification wording are flagged for Consultant and oncology-pharmacy review; patients should never change the dose themselves.
contraception: Discuss fertility before treatment. Effective contraception is needed during treatment and for six months after the final dose for women who could become pregnant, and for three months for male patients with female partners who could become pregnant. Do not breastfeed during treatment; the EU product information also advises against breastfeeding for one month after the last dose.

logistics.title: Plan two visits per cycle
logistics.text: Day 1 and Day 8 are treatment days. Allow time for blood review, premedicines, the infusion and at least 30 minutes of observation afterwards. The first infusion is longer than later ones.

logistics.title: Cannula or existing venous access
logistics.text: The team chooses suitable intravenous access. A port is not automatically required and this regimen has no take-home pump. If you already have a port, staff access and flush it according to local policy; report pain, redness or swelling.

logistics.title: Before leaving the unit
logistics.text: Confirm the Day 8 appointment, blood-test arrangements, nausea medicines, written diarrhoea instructions and the number to call if unwell. If G-CSF is prescribed, ask exactly which days to take it around both treatment visits.

logistics.title: If treatment is delayed
logistics.text: A low count or significant side effect can mean a delay or dose change. The team will give the revised plan; do not calculate a replacement infusion from this diagram.

logistics.title: If radiotherapy is also planned
logistics.text: Radiotherapy is not an automatic phase of this advanced-disease regimen. If needed for local symptoms or another reason, the oncology and radiotherapy teams agree its timing and any treatment interruption.

support.title: Prevent nausea before both doses
support.text: This is a high-emetic-risk regimen. Preventive antiemetics are needed for both Day 1 and Day 8, with take-home medicines and clear instructions. The steroid used as an infusion premedicine also provides antiemetic cover, so the team must reconcile the total dose.

support.title: A written diarrhoea plan
support.text: Report diarrhoea early. The team assesses infection, dehydration and electrolyte loss, and supplies an appropriate antidiarrhoeal prescription. Follow the written oncology instructions; do not improvise repeated high doses of loperamide.

support.title: Blood-count support
support.text: G-CSF injections may be considered from cycle 1 if the risk of febrile neutropenia is increased, or after significant neutropenia. Product and timing depend on the two-infusion schedule and the prescribing plan.

support.title: Infusion-reaction prevention
support.text: The unit gives premedicines to reduce reaction risk and observes you during and after each infusion. Tell staff immediately if you feel different or unwell.

support.title: Early cramping or diarrhoea during an infusion
support.text: This can be an acute cholinergic effect and needs staff assessment. Atropine may be used for later infusions when appropriate; tell the team if you have glaucoma.

agents.name: Sacituzumab govitecan (Trodelvy)
agents.mechanism: Carries the topoisomerase-I inhibitor SN-38 using an antibody that recognises Trop-2
agents.explanation: The antibody component recognises Trop-2 on cancer cells. Its linked SN-38 payload interferes with topoisomerase I, an enzyme involved in managing DNA during copying, which can damage dividing cells. Healthy tissues can also be affected, particularly blood-forming cells and the gut; being antibody-directed does not mean it is free of chemotherapy-type effects.
agents.watch: The most important early problems to act on are fever or infection with low neutrophils, diarrhoea and dehydration, persistent nausea/vomiting, and infusion reactions. Report symptoms early rather than waiting for a planned scan or clinic.
risks: Low neutrophils and serious infection, including febrile neutropenia
Diarrhoea, dehydration and electrolyte loss; sometimes kidney injury
Infusion reactions, including rare life-threatening reactions
Potential harm to an unborn baby and effects on fertility

anatomy: Fever, shivering or suddenly feeling unwell needs immediate oncology advice; a low neutrophil count itself may cause no symptoms.
Report loose stools early, especially with cramps, fever, dizziness or reduced urine. Follow the prescribed diarrhoea plan.
Use preventive medicines for both infusion days. Contact the team if you cannot keep fluids down.
Tell the team about limiting tiredness, breathlessness or dizziness; blood tests help identify anaemia and other causes.
Hair thinning or loss can occur; ask about practical scalp and appearance support.
Tell staff immediately about rash, swelling, breathing difficulty or faintness during treatment.

evidence.title: ASCENT — Bardia et al., NEJM 2021
evidence.population: Randomised open-label phase III trial, 529 patients with previously treated metastatic TNBC. The primary efficacy population comprised 468 patients without baseline brain metastases; ECOG was 0–1.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review in the population without baseline brain metastases.
evidence.interpretation: In the primary population, median PFS was 5.6 versus 1.7 months (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.32–0.52) and median OS was 12.1 versus 6.7 months (HR 0.48, 95% CI 0.38–0.59) with sacituzumab versus physician-choice chemotherapy. Response was 35% versus 5%.
evidence.limitations: The primary analysis excluded baseline brain metastases; the overall-population estimates differ. Open-label design, selected trial fitness and previous-treatment requirements limit extrapolation. Group medians do not predict an individual patient's benefit. This trial does not establish eligibility for every broader current EU indication.

cycle_rows.text: Blood review, premedicines, infusion and observation

cycle_rows.label: Day 8 infusion
cycle_rows.text: Reassess symptoms and ANC, then premedicines, infusion and observation

cycle_rows.label: Nausea / bowel symptoms
cycle_rows.text: May occur after either dose or between visits. This is a watch window, not a predicted symptom period.

cycle_rows.label: Blood-count / infection watch
cycle_rows.text: Risk varies across the cycle; fever or feeling unwell needs urgent advice on any day.

cycle_rows.label: Energy / recovery
cycle_rows.text: Fatigue may fluctuate or build over repeated cycles. No planned infusion on Day 15 does not guarantee absence of side effects.

clinical_notes: NCCP00794a is later-line unresectable/metastatic TNBC. Do not import current EU HR-positive, first-line or pembrolizumab-combination indications without the appropriate separate NCCP/reimbursement mapping.
Day 1 ANC threshold is ≥1.5 ×10⁹/L; Day 8 is ≥1.0 ×10⁹/L. An isolated ANC <1.0 can trigger a hold without a day; 1.0–<1.5 requires day context rather than a false clearance.

NCCP high-emetic-risk prophylaxis must cover BOTH Day 1 and Day 8. The suggested dexamethasone 12 mg infusion premedicine also provides antiemetic cover; reconcile with the selected high-risk script to prevent duplication.

NCCP suggested infusion premedicines: paracetamol 1 g PO 60 minutes beforehand; chlorphenamine 10 mg IV, famotidine 20 mg IV and dexamethasone 12 mg PO 30 minutes beforehand. Product availability, contraindications and local prescriptions must be checked.

Primary G-CSF should be considered from cycle 1 for increased-risk patients in the current EU SmPC. Product and timing must account for Day 1 and Day 8; do not automatically generate a single generic pegfilgrastim date.

NCCP advises considering a lower initial dose for known UGT1A1*28 homozygosity and possible escalation based on cycle-1 tolerance, but gives no fixed starting reduction. The EU SmPC recommends close monitoring and does not require routine genotype testing when status is unknown. Do not re-escalate a dose previously reduced because of adverse reactions.

NCCP Table 1 repeats 25% dose reduction at the second severe non-neutropenic event, whereas the current EU SmPC gives a 10→7.5→5 mg/kg ladder. The second-event output requires Consultant/pharmacy reconciliation and suppresses automatic numeric dosing.

NCCP Table 2 predicts no renal/hepatic adjustment across broad impairment bands. EU SmPC advises avoiding use when bilirubin >1.5×ULN or AST/ALT >3×ULN without liver metastases or >5×ULN with metastases, and notes absent severe/end-stage renal data. These differences are explicit in the assessment output.

NCCP contains >48-hour and >3-week toxicity-duration rules that differ from the current EU algorithm. Persisting severe toxicity must not be treated by merely calculating a reduced dose; recovery and source reconciliation are required.

NCCP's high-dose loperamide schedule is 4 mg initially then 2 mg every two hours, continued 12 hours after the last liquid stool and never beyond 48 consecutive hours at these doses because of ileus risk. The patient-facing page should direct to an individually prescribed local oncology plan rather than print an unsupervised automatic prescription. Assess infectious causes, fever, blood, severe pain and dehydration promptly.
Scan timing is Consultant-plan-specific; no universal three-month CT or tumour-marker schedule is specified in NCCP00794. Routine ECG/echo/DXA should not be added merely to fill a timeline.
Software source reconciliation and 143 scenario/structure checks do not constitute independent Consultant or oncology-pharmacy validation.
